structured_output.summary: Pulsator with -1523 ppm P/2 modulation and sector depths p 7e-14; Sectors 112-114 decide.
reasons: Disagree with the mechanical 'proposed for submission'. The step 9 row in the input is empty because of error 'HTTPError: Error 503: Server overloaded' (verification_date_utc 2026-11-01 22:30), so the mechanical rules were applied without the all-sector values; the verification record holds a complete earlier run (2026-10-31 09:08, code version a039af5, verdict passed) and I use those values below.

The target itself is a known pulsator: vsx_variables lists Gaia DR3 6064573197263477376 DSCT|GDOR|SXPHE at 0". The record's step 9 run finds a coherent modulation at half the candidate period of ellipsoidal -1523 +/- 118 ppm (13 sigma; companion mass not detected). The negative sign is unphysical for ellipsoidal variation and the amplitude is 1.8 times the fit depth of 863 +/- 56 ppm, so a gamma Dor/delta Scuti mode near 2/P (about 2.72 c/d) is the likely origin, and a pulsation-driven false alarm at period_days 0.735052 cannot be excluded. The pipeline raised no caution for it.

Per-sector depths from the QLP light curves are inconsistent: sector depths S102 1874 +/- 167, S11 1464 +/- 218, S38 857 +/- 154, S65 535 +/- 162, S99 837 +/- 176, S100 824 +/- 152, S101 123 +/- 147 (p 7.08e-14). S101 is consistent with zero, and the S102 depth that triggered the search is about twice the joint fit depth. The all-sector figure shows a clear dip in S102, S11, S38, S99 and S100, a weak one in S65 and none in S101, which fits a transit beating against stellar variability as well as it fits a planet.

Other-sector evidence is uniformly weaker than predicted: other_sector_results gives S65 SNR 8.8 vs expected 12.9, S99 9.4 vs 13.0, S100 10.5 vs 14.8, S101 12.4 vs 14.4; joint_search_snr 8.4 (joint_search_detected True, joint_search_highest_null_snr 5.0) is lower than the single-sector S102 BLS SNR 12.3 in the record, as expected if the apparent depth varies between sectors.

Localisation supports the target but rests on one sector: pixel_verdicts_by_sector gives S102 on target (SNR 7.3) and S100 unresolved (SNR 5.5, best star TIC 457325371); S11, S38, S65, S99 and S101 are too faint and the best star wanders among unrelated neighbours. The joint_pixel_verdict is on target with joint_difference_image_snr 9.7 and joint_best_source TIC 457325371. The S102 and S100 difference images do peak on the target. The field is crowded: gaia_neighbours 176, with 33 stars in gaia_neighbours_able_to_cause_dip, the closest Gaia DR3 6064573197263478784 at 12" G 17.6 needing 40% and Gaia DR3 6064573197267811968 at 34" G 14.3 needing only 2%; this is the only pipeline caution ('neighbour able to cause dip').

Evidence in favour that keeps this from a drop: triceratops_verdict likely planet with fpp_mean 0.0377 +/- 0.0012 and nfpp_mean 0 (nearby_scenarios_excluded True, most_likely_scenario TP on TIC 457325371); record step 9 gives odd-even 0.75 sigma, secondary 160 +/- 68 ppm below the planet maximum of 289 ppm, Gaia RV variable False with companion mass below 0.0494 solar masses, density ratio 1.24; gaia_ruwe 0.93 and gaia_non_single_star 0.

Not a star by size: record step 9 gives Rp 5.83 +/- 0.32 Earth radii with b 0.388 and transit_grazing False (companion_radius_earth_radii 6.51328 from step 7), well below 22.4 Earth radii. A 5.8 Earth-radius body at period_days 0.735 would be a rare ultra-short-period sub-Saturn, plausible but unusual enough to want the variability question settled first.

No catalogue conflict: exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are empty, ephemeris_match_likely_sources is empty, and released_tess_sectors_not_in_all_sector_verification is empty, so the signal would be new if real.

What would decide it: unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 112 113 114 add three sectors for the per-sector depth test and the pixel check. If the dip recurs at fit_period_days 0.7349930 and fit_epoch_btjd 4077.68167 with depth near 863 ppm in all three sectors and the difference image again peaks on the target, submit; if depths again swing between ~0 and ~1900 ppm, drop as pulsation beating. Sooner, a rerun of step 9 (the 503 was transient) plus a periodogram showing whether a pulsation mode sits at 1/P or 2/P (about 1.36 or 2.72 c/d) would decide it.
